title: Metrics for many customers
like: a shared metrics service like Mimir
brief: Build one metrics platform for 5,000 customers. A tenant can create millions of series or run a costly month-long query by mistake. Your design must preserve useful ingestion and query service for the other tenants, and show the offending customer a clear limit rather than an unexplained gap.

clarify.a: The normal fleet has about 10 million active series at a 15-second interval, roughly 667,000 samples/s. The peak plan is 720,000 samples/s. A telemetry request is a catalog batch of 100 samples (approx.).

Enforce active-series, new-series and samples/s quotas plus label size on writes. Limit query concurrency, time range, scanned samples and wall time separately. Global requests/s is only a coarse admission guard.

Use weighted fair queues with bounded waiting, and shuffle-sharded ingest subsets inside independent cells. Cell-local data paths should isolate a failure. Shared identity and control-plane dependencies must be included in the blast-radius analysis.

Normal query visibility should be within a minute. Dashboards may cache stable ranges for a minute, but alert evaluations need a separate fresh path. Keep 14 days of full detail, then preserve semantics-aware aggregates under a separate policy.

notes: Storage planning uses the normal steady rate: 10 million/15 × 1.5 B × 86,400 × 14 days ≈ 1.2096 TB compressed payload, before indexes, recent WAL and replica copies (approx.).
The Time-series database element includes recent data and historical object blocks. The graph does not draw a fake store-to-store link.

The shared API coordinates ingest and query requests. The sim does not model per-tenant weights, cardinality memory, new-series churn or cell assignment. The cardinality event affects the platform's own Metrics observer bill.

The current sim applies a global request mix. All source paths share a real authenticated front door. workloadPlan records source-specific rates for a later engine; it is descriptive and does not affect this score.

numbers.label: Normal full-detail payload
numbers.how: 10 million/15 samples/s × 1.5 B × 86,400 × 14 days, before metadata (approx.).

numbers.label: Tenant active-state allowance
numbers.how: Assume 100,000 active series/tenant × 2 KB state/series, before sample buffers (approx.).

hints: Separate series count from sample count. Which customer can exhaust memory without sending more bytes?
Set tenant budgets for writes and reads independently, then schedule fairly. A limiter alone cannot prove fairness.

Use three-zone replicated ingestion and a WAL inside the time-series store, immutable object blocks, tenant-aware cached reads and an uncached alert path. Work through shuffle overlap and shared dependencies before claiming cell isolation.

editorial.summary: Hash tenant and series identity onto a replicated ingest ring and durably record the acknowledged data. Flush blocks to object storage, compact them and expire by policy. Split long queries into bounded tasks with fair scheduling. Enforce tenant limits before expensive allocation and again on actual query work. The reference uses the catalog's integrated time-series store. It measures aggregate headroom during capacity loss, not the correctness of tenant scheduling or cardinality accounting.

designs.name: Shared admission and a three-zone time-series fleet
designs.why: Both sources enter one authentic front door. The API contains distributors and query coordination; the integrated store contains WAL, recent samples and historical blocks. Read caching is tenant-aware by design; report/alert evaluations stay on the uncached path in this graph. No link connects agents to an unrelated query service to satisfy the current global mix.

tradeoffs: R = W = 2 of a fixed three-replica set intersects, but version handling and a defined protocol are still required. Zone placement affects write latency and recovery bandwidth.

A 100,000-series quota at an assumed 2 KB per active series is about 200 MB state per tenant before replication. Multiply only actual active series, not every tenant's unused quota reservation, unless the product guarantees reserved capacity.
Use tenant ids in cache keys and authorization checks. A cache improves repeated dashboard reads, but alert freshness needs a separate policy.
Shuffle sharding reduces repeated overlap; it does not remove overlap. With 2 of 10 workers, identical pairs occur with probability 1/45, but any overlap occurs with probability 17/45.

Cells contain only failures whose dependencies remain cell-local. Independent storage, queues and staged deploys cost spare capacity but reduce reach. A common critical key service can still affect everyone.
editorial.realWorld: The catalog models about 300,000 samples/s written per ingest node as 3,000 batches of 100, and about 500 range queries/s per node. Replication, series churn, query width, zone loss and recovery mean dividing the peak by 300,000 is only a starting point (approx.).

correctness.prompt: A tenant stays within samples/s but creates a new series on every request and runs wide queries. Which independent budgets protect the other 4,999 customers?
correctness.discussion: Authenticate the tenant, cap label size, active series and new-series rate before allocating unbounded state, and return explicit limit feedback. Query work needs separate concurrency, range, scanned-sample and time limits. Carry tenant identity through fair queues and cancellation. Include tenant scope in caches and data authorization. Cell and shuffle placement reduce shared failure reach only if critical dependencies follow the same boundary.

fields.label: Write admission
options: Active series, churn, label size and samples/s
fields.explanation: Low byte rates can still create expensive metadata.

fields.label: Read fairness
options: Bound and fairly schedule query work per tenant
Put every tenant in one unlimited FIFO
fields.explanation: A single FIFO lets broad queries delay cheap work from other tenants.

correctness.limits: The aggregate traffic score does not prove per-tenant isolation, authorization, cardinality handling or fair scheduling.
